title: Kerala Monsoon Death Toll Rises to Eight as Floods and Landslides Ravage State
excerpt: Two children among the dead as near-cloudburst conditions trigger flash floods and landslides across central Kerala, with over 5,700 people sheltering in relief camps and eight still missing.
body:
• At least eight people killed in rain-related incidents across Kerala since August 1, including two children swept away by overflowing streams in Malappuram district.
  • Over 5,700 people displaced and sheltering in relief camps, with eight people still missing as search operations continue in multiple districts.
  • IMD red alerts issued for nine districts warning of extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 200 mm in 24 hours; rivers Pamba, Manimala, and Meenachil have overflowed their banks.
  • Chief Minister V D Satheesan has directed ministers to remain in affected districts and coordinate relief, with NDRF teams deployed across the state.

The death toll from Kerala's monsoon fury has climbed to eight after near-cloudburst conditions triggered devastating flash floods and landslides across the state's central districts over the weekend. Two children drowned in separate incidents in Malappuram district, according to Onmanorama, adding to six deaths reported from landslides in Idukki, Kottayam, and Wayanad on Saturday.

Eight people remain missing and at least 13 have been injured, according to state disaster management officials cited by the Times of India. More than 5,700 displaced residents are sheltering in relief camps, a number that has grown sharply from the 1,465 reported in 65 camps just hours earlier on Saturday.

Landslides Claim Lives Across Central Kerala

The deadliest incidents occurred in Idukki and Kottayam districts. In Kudayathoor near Thodupuzha, 69-year-old Sumathi was killed when a portion of a hill caved in and buried her house around 2 am on Saturday. Her husband Ravi Narayanan, 72, and son Ratheesh, 38, were rescued with injuries by a 29-member NDRF team, according to the New Indian Express.

In Vagamon, Prabhakaran Nair, 72, died after a landslide sent mud crashing through the room where he was sleeping at a relative's house. In Poonjar, Kottayam district, Josephine Johny, 28, and his mother Rejina Johny were both killed when debris struck their home around 4:30 am. A 57-year-old farmer, Mankott Benny, was found dead near a pond on his farmland in Wayanad, suspected to have been electrocuted while operating a water pump.

"A 24-hour alert has to be observed and all those living close to water sources have to be very cautious. Travel in hilly areas should be best avoided and areas prone to landslides have also to be watchful."

— V D Satheesan, Kerala Chief Minister

Extreme Rainfall After Months of Deficit

The deluge arrived after a prolonged dry spell. Kerala experienced a 34% monsoon rainfall deficit during June and July before an offshore trough and localized atmospheric depressions combined to trigger extreme precipitation. Vagamon recorded 31.4 cm of rainfall within eight hours, while Vadasserikkara in Pathanamthitta received 33 cm, the New Indian Express reported.

Rivers including the Pamba, Manimala, and Meenachil have overflowed their banks. Ranni town in Pathanamthitta was submerged as the Pampa river breached its banks. Authorities opened dam shutters at Pambla, Kallarkutty, and Malankara due to heavy inflow.

Rescue Operations and Displacement

The state government has deployed NDRF teams, police, fire services, and Coast Guard personnel across affected regions. Chief Minister Satheesan directed ministers in charge of rain-hit districts to remain in their areas and oversee operations.

"We have already opened relief camps wherever required. Even if the intensity of the rain decreases, people living in high-risk areas will be shifted to camps as a precautionary measure."

— A P Anilkumar, Kerala Revenue Minister

A complete ban on tourism was imposed in Idukki district, and authorities enforced a night traffic ban on the Boys Town–Palchuram Road connecting Kannur and Wayanad. Multiple roads were blocked by landslides, and traffic on the Kochi-Dhanushkodi National Highway was disrupted near Cheeyapara.

Echoes of 2018 and a Diaspora on Alert

The scenes have drawn comparisons to Kerala's catastrophic 2018 floods, which killed 483 people and displaced over a million. For Kerala's large diaspora — an estimated 2.1 million Keralites live abroad, concentrated in the Gulf states, the US, and the UK — the footage of submerged towns and rescue boats is grimly familiar. During the 2018 disaster, overseas Keralites mobilized massive fundraising efforts, and diaspora networks are already closely monitoring the unfolding crisis.

What's Next

The IMD has maintained red alerts for nine districts, forecasting extremely heavy rainfall in isolated areas. Orange alerts are in place for Ernakulam, Thrissur, and Palakkad. With dam reservoirs filling rapidly and rivers continuing to swell, the state faces the prospect of further flooding if rains persist. Search operations for the eight missing people continue, and the death toll could rise as rescue teams reach more remote areas.
nri_angle: Kerala's 2.1 million-strong diaspora, concentrated in the Gulf, US, and UK, is monitoring the crisis closely, drawing comparisons to the devastating 2018 floods that triggered massive overseas fundraising.
author: Diaspora Desk
